_: NEW-78: what the speech worker does with the microphone while push to talk is held, before any client draws it. Only the voice device listens, so ONE implementation replays this (apps/desktop/crates/voice/src/listen.rs); the clients ×4 draw the `level` events (VoiceWave, NEW-54 b2) and never recompute them. Audio is mono 16 kHz in frames of 512 samples (32 ms, Silero's frame): every frame yields one `level` event (`level` + 8 `bands`, each 0..1, rounded to 3 decimals). A frame's level = its RMS in dBFS mapped linearly from floorDb (0) to ceilingDb (1), clamped; a band's level = the same mapping of the RMS of its share of a Hann-windowed spectrum (bandEdgesHz, log-spaced). The drawn value moves towards the measured one by `attack` per frame when rising and by `release` when falling. Speech = Silero probabilities per frame: a segment opens at a frame >= threshold, a run of frames below negThreshold starts the silence (frames between the two thresholds keep the segment open), minSilenceMs of silence closes it, a segment with less than minSpeechMs of speech is dropped, padMs of audio is kept on both sides (never reaching back into the previous segment), and a segment is cut at maxSegmentMs. Releasing the key closes the open segment where the speech ended. Every closed segment is transcribed at once (Parakeet), so release waits only for the last; on a GPU the open segment is re-transcribed every partialEveryMs for `partial` (never on the CPU). Transcripts are normalised (whitespace collapsed, no space before . , ! ? ; : % ), nothing without a letter or digit) and the segments joined with one space: empty = `empty`, else `heard`.

wake._: #NEW-56 (voice plan V7, approved 2026-10-27): the wake word, with NO wake-word model. While it is on (the voice device, an agent picked, Wake word on, the tray's Mute off) the speech worker keeps the microphone open and Silero scoring it (the segment rules above); in silence that is all it does. The start of every speech segment is transcribed ONCE by the resident Parakeet, a window sized to the phrase (`window`: windowBaseMs + windowPerLetterMs × the phrase's letters, clamped to windowMinMs … windowMaxMs; `Hey Studio` = 9 letters = 1500 ms; owner decision 2026-10-27: a 2 s window cost 29 % of a CPU core under continuous talk): as soon as the open segment is that long, or when a shorter segment closes (`checks`: [start, end) in frames, padding included, one per segment; a dropped segment is never checked; a segment cut at maxSegmentMs is a new segment). MATCH (`match`): the transcript's `words` are its runs of letters and digits, lowercased, the accents Parakeet writes folded to ASCII (ä→a, ö→o, ü→u, ß→ss, é→e …), an apostrophe joining (What's = whats), anything else separating. The phrase (Settings → Voice `wakePhrase`, empty = `Hey {agent}`) must OPEN the segment: its letters with the spaces dropped are compared (Levenshtein) with the transcript's first 1 … n+2 words joined (n = the phrase's words), the closest wins, and it matches within floor(letters × maxEditRatio) edits (`Hey Studio` = 9 letters = 2 edits; a 5-letter phrase tolerates 1, so `Hey Al` hears `Hey all`: pick a longer name). A phrase without a letter or digit never matches. `rest` = the text after the matched words, leading punctuation and spaces dropped, its first letter capitalised (null = no match). TURN: a match is a push-to-talk key-down for one turn (worker event `woke`, then the same level / partial / heard / empty as a Listen, the capsule ×1): the segment from its padded start seeds the utterance, everything heard is joined as above and loses the phrase (`rest` again; unchanged when the longer transcript no longer opens with it), and the worker ends the turn itself (`turn`): never while a segment is open, after turnEndMs of quiet (since the last segment's padded end) once a command was heard, after noCommandMs while only the phrase was (empty: a false wake costs one capsule and sends nothing), and at maxTurnMs regardless. A push-to-talk key-down replaces a running turn (no answer for it) and borrows the open microphone; the wake word resumes after every turn and Listen. NO SELF-WAKE (#1263 review): while a reply is being spoken, and for echoTailMs after it ends, every frame the microphone hears counts as the reply's: a segment whose padded start falls among those frames is never checked (no transcription), so the agent's own voice can neither wake it nor barge in on itself; a phrase said after the reply wakes as usual. Wake word off (or Mute) ends a wake turn in flight in the worker, unanswered, and a `woke` that reaches the host after the wake word was taken back is cancelled there (CancelListen), never sent.
